card.statement:
Note that the assumption that $\mathrm{char}(\mathbf{k})=0$ is crucial here. The category ${\mathord{\mathrm{P}_{\mathscr{S}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})}}$ with $\mathbf{k}$ a field of positive characteristic is not semisimple.

The strata $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\lambda}$ of $\mathscr{S}$ are simply connected, because they are affine bundles over partial flag varieties (see Proposition 3.2). Thus, the only simple
local system on $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\lambda}$ is the trivial local system $\underline{\mathbf{k}}$ . We denote by
${\mathbf{IC}}_{\lambda}$ the corresponding intersection cohomology sheaf. Then,
the simple objects in ${\mathord{\mathrm{P}_{\mathscr{S}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})}}$ are (up to isomorphism) these complexes ${\mathbf{IC}}_{\lambda}$ ,
for $\lambda\in X_{*}(T)^{+}$ . Since every object in ${\mathord{\mathrm{P}_{\mathscr{S}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})}}$ has finite length, and in view of (4.1), Theorem 4.2 follows from the following claim.
card.label: Remark 4.3

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
